## BOOK 1 of 2: "Bindle: Some Chapters in the Life of Joseph Bindle" (Herbert Jenkins, 1916, Gutenberg 33261)
Epigraph: T. P. O'Connor, M.P.: Bindle "greatest Cockney... since Dickens wrote Pickwick Papers." Dedication: "To My Mother." Foreword: author H.J.; Blackwood suggestion; a publisher-as-author joke.

Chapters (21):
I. The Bindles at Home – Bindle & Ginger at the Blue Boar (Hammersmith); Bindle's "tack," "Gospel Bells," tin of salmon; Ginger's "three babies"; Bindle's father drank "to keep the chill out," "wet 'is 'air" after chapel. Bindle: journeyman furniture-remover, little, bald, red nose, Fenton Street (Fulham), half-house; loves beer & "little jokes." Mrs. Bindle (Lizzie): sour, cleanliness/religion, Alton Road Chapel, "Got a job?", tin bath episode (Bindle rubbed boots in bath), "Gospel Bells." Mrs. Bindle's sister Martha married Alfred Hearty (greengrocer, Fulham High Street, "'oly smile"). Bindle lies he has night-watchman job at a garage; pawns Mrs. B's travelling clock (7s) to pay lodging; she calls him "yer great hulkin' brute"; "Steal!" idea.
II. A Nocturnal Adventure – Keys of Professor Sylvanus Conti (13 Audrey Mansions, Queen's Club, W. Kensington; reward 2s 6d) found; duplicated at stall (1s 3d/1s); Bindle bandaged head disguise; Conti's hypnotist/mesmerist career, rival "John Gibson, the English Mesmerist"; Bindle caught in flat, handcuffed; Conti hypnotises him, writes letter to police; Bindle delivers it to a workman who takes it to police.
III. The Hypnotic Fiasco – Bindle walks, coffee-stall; police-station; Conti's charge fails in West London Police Court; magistrate; Conti's reputation lost; watch/property returned by post; Evening Post headline "THE GREAT HYPNOTIC FIASCO."
IV. The Heartys at Home – Mr. Alfred Hearty (whiskers, lemons, "pull for the shore"), Mrs. Martha Hearty (fat, wheezes), Millie (18), Bindle's "Pull for the Shore" sabotage; Bindle's missionary double-bed story; Millie asks to go to pictures (Friday).
V. Bindle Tries a Change of Work – Splendid Hotel night painting; foreman (Sanders) insults; Bindle removes No. 1 East door numbers and swaps them; chambermaid remark.
VI. The Hotel Corridor – Mixed-up rooms (clergyman, Frenchman "vingt-quatre," monocled Army man, "Mon Dieu"); deputy-manager; fireman; Mrs. Bindle attacks foreman Sanders with broom/dishcloth, he says "God forgive me."
VII. Bindle Commits an Indiscretion – Bindle escorts Millie to Putney Pavilion; meets Charlie Dixon (shipping office, grey eyes); Bindle as cupid; Millie's bump into Mr. Hearty; Bindle's church-bench speech about "Gawd."
VIII. The Great Conspiracy – Harridge's Stores; Barton Bridge Temperance Fete (Society 25th anniversary; Sir John Bilder's ale; Lady Knob-Kerrick; Dr. Little; Dick Little); Bindle mixes alcohol into lemonade via Dick Little's flask.
IX. The Temperance Fete – chaos, Rev. Andrew McFie (Congregational, Scot), Mr. Slocum (vicar), Miss Slocum, Miss McFie, Mr. Wace, Mr. Marsh, Mr. Grint; fire-hose by Saunders; police (superintendent from Ryford); Bindle drives off horses/carriages; Dick Little offers sovereign.
X. Mr. Hearty Prays for Bindle – Mrs. B: "Mr. Hearty prayed for you… a wheat-ear among thorns"; Bindle at Dick Little's flat (Beaufort Mansions), Tim's hospital friends; Bindle's "speech" from table.
XI. Mr. Hearty Becomes Extremely Unpopular – Lily the dog (advertisement "Dog wanted… Alfred Hearty… Saturday 10.30"); crowds for housekeeper/errand boy/adoptions; Bindle sends vans; Hearty gives Bindle a pineapple.
XII. Bindle Agrees to Become a Millionaire – Reginald Graves (St. Joseph's College, Oxford; "Gravy"; grocer's son; Josiah Williams, Australian uncle); Tom Little, Dick Travers, Guggers (gug-gug stammer); Oxford Mail notice.
XIII. Oxford's Welcome to Bindle – Bindle as Josiah Williams of Moonagoona, Sceptre hotel; kangaroo (Horace Trent, cox); Bungem's dinner; asparagus; Dr. Peter (Master); Graves's humiliation; Bindle's speech on Graves's grocer father Tom Graves, Bingley; Bushmen war-cry.
XIV. Mr. Hearty Gives a Party – Sopley (pastor), Rev. Edward Winch (missionary), Flinders, "Here we go looping"; Bindle's vote of thanks; Mr. Hearty's cut pineapple.
XV. Bindle and the German Menace – Little Compton, Suffolk; Holmleigh; Mr. Henry Miller's firearms; Mr. John Gandy (Dove and Easel); Sir Charles Custance; Sergeant Wrannock; Mr. Greenhales; Mr. Roger Greenhales; Mrs. Grinder; foreman Brooks; Sergeant trapped; Mr. Miller's arms.
XVI. The Amateur Detectives – foreman catches Wrannock, Greenhales, Gandy, Custance; police arrive; "Charles Peace" joke.
XVII. Bindle Makes a Mistake – West London Furniture Depository; Branksome Road No. 181 vs 131; Rogers family (Railton-Rogers, 7 children, Eustace, Nelly, Muriel); Mr. and Mrs. Granger at 33 Lebanon Avenue, Chiswick; Bindle dismissed.
XVIII. Bindle Assists in an Elopement – Kitchener's Army refusal (varicose veins); special constable; Dick Little & Ethel Knob-Kerrick elopement; Guggers' Rolls-Royce; Lady Knob-Kerrick, Miss Strint, Thomas, Wilton; £5 compensation.
XIX. The Scarlet Horse Coterie – Ginger enlists; Ruddy Bill, Wilkes, Huggles, Tom Cave, Weary, Ted; War talk.
XX. Millie Leaves Home – Hearty's clash; Millie goes to Aunt Lizzie; "Lizzie, I'll go to chapel Sunday."
XXI. Conclusion – Dick Little & Ettie marry; Bindle says "Funny things, women"; Mrs. Little.

## BOOK 2 of 2: "Adventures of Bindle" (Herbert Jenkins, Gutenberg 32285)
Dedication: "To the Children of the Dead End."
Chapters (16):
I. The Coming of the Lodger – Mrs. B answers ad in The Gospel Sentinel ("Lonely"); lodger Mr. Josiah Gupperduck (accordion, Society for Suppression of Atheism, bald, red nose, large round spectacles, false teeth); Bindle's "Gawd."
II. A Downing Street Sensation – Empson & Daley; horses; Tippitt (cigarette); Merton van; suffragettes ("Black and White Raiders") in pantechnicon; lamp-black via watering-can; Chief-Inspector Gunny of Scotland Yard; Llewellyn John, 110 Downing Street.
III. The Air-Raid – Mr. Hearty, Gupperduck cowering in potato-cellar; scales dropped; Mrs. Bindle faints; Millie's Charlie at front.
IV. The Duplication of Mr. Hearty – six duplicates of Hearty ("alibis"); Mrs. Hearty laughs; Hearty's third shop in Putney High Street.
V. The Gathering of the Bands – donkeys with sandwich boards, camel, rival brass bands; police inspector.
VI. Mr. Gupperduck's Mishap – Peace meeting in Hyde Park, Gupperduck beaten, Peter (sandy beard) up a tree; Mrs. B nursing; Bindle refuses him.
VII. The Courting of the Rev. Andrew MacFie – MacFie (Scots, new Alton Road pastor) courts Millie; Miss MacFie; Bindle's Uriah/David joke; Lady Knob-Kerrick.
VIII. The Chapel Conversazione – Heartys' party for Sopley's retirement; glee-party "The Glad Eye"; Mrs. Pain, Mr. & Mrs. Withers, Tuddenham & Muskett, Miss Torkington; woman claiming to be MacFie's wife; police whistle by John; Dick Little's "Nancy" disguise.
IX. The Letting of Number Six – Bindle as caretaker at Fulham Square Mansions for Charlie Hart; Mrs. Sedge ("Royal Richard" gin); Number Seven; "Queenie" (maid, No. 8); Miss Cissie Boye (No. 6); Jabez Stiffson.
X. The Downfall of Mr. Jabez Stiffson – Stiffson in Cissie's bath; Mrs. Stiffson (Oscar the canary); porridge bowl on Stiffson's head; Mrs. Stiffson stuck in lift.
XI. The Camouflaging of Mr. Gupperduck – Ginger; Mrs. B: Gupperduck injured at peace meeting; "camelflage."
XII. The Tragedy of Giuseppi Antonio Tolmenicino – Scratcher; Napolini's (Regent St) waiter; Mr. James Smith (Herr Siegesmann) superintendent; Italian arrested as spy.
XIII. The Return of Charlie Dixon – Charlie home on leave; Universal Cafe; champagne "Number 68"; Millie and Charlie marry; "Uncle Joe."
XIV. Mr. Hearty Yields – Bindle's bluff about Hearty's illicit history with "Six-an'-Eightpence" (fabricated); Hearty agrees to marriage Tuesday.
XV. A Billeting Adventure – Harridge's van, Ginger, Wilkes, Huggles; Lady Knob-Kerrick's drawing-room; sixteen soldiers; red herring; "various veins."
XVI. Millie's Wedding – Hearty's hat under carriage; Rev. Sopley officiates; Mr. Dixon (Charlie's uncle, "Beer!"); Bindle's toast; Mrs. Dixon: "you must be a very good man."
